title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, inferred from the neighbouring pages. Λ = Z/4Z and M is a free Λ-module of rank 2, the 4-torsion of an elliptic curve. So Gl_Λ(M) ≅ GL_2(Z/4), of order 96, and Sl_Λ(M) is the index-2 subgroup with det = 1, of order 48. The objects are:
- I is the affine plane over F_2 on M_0 = M/2M, with 4 points, so S_I ≅ S_4 and S_I^+ ≅ A_4.
- J is the set of 3 lines, so S_J ≅ GL_2(F_2) ≅ S_3.
- D_Q is a dihedral group of order 8 attached to a quadratic form Q.
- D_Q^+ ⊂ D_Q is its cyclic subgroup of order 4. Its centre z_Q = {1, e_Q} has order 2.

The previous page showed that the canonical map Gl_Λ(M) → D_Q is surjective with kernel S_I^+ ≅ A_4. This kernel equals [Sl, Sl], of index 4 in Sl. Hence Sl_ab ≅ D_Q^+ ≅ Z/4, and det factors through D_Q → {±1}.

Diagram (25) is a 3×3 'star' of short exact sequences centred on Sl_Λ(M), not Gl. The image shows 𝔖l_Λ(M) at the centre.
- Top: the normal subgroup S_I^+ × Z, with Z = {1, −id_M}, of order 24. pr_1 and pr_2 go to S_I^+ and to Z.
- Z maps isomorphically onto z_Q = {1, e_Q} ≅ F_2.
- Left column: 1 → Z → Sl → S_I → 1. Reduction gives a surjection Sl → S_4 whose kernel is the scalars ±1.
- Right column: 1 → S_I^+ → Sl → D_Q^+ → 1.
- Bottom: S_I →sg {±1} has kernel S_I^+. D_Q^+ → {±1} has kernel z_Q. The vertical map Sl → {±1} (labelled 'cont') has kernel S_I^+ × Z.
Compatibility says the sign of the S_4-image of g ∈ Sl equals the reduction mod 2 of the Z/4-valued abelianization character.

Corollary 2. Gl_Λ(M) → D_Q induces Gl_ab = Gl/(S_I^+ × Z) ≅ (D_Q)_ab = D_Q/z_Q. This is a 2-dimensional F_2-vector space, canonically F_2 × F_2. Here Z = Cent(Gl_Λ(M)) maps onto Cent(D_Q).

The NB identifies the three nontrivial characters of the dihedral quotient with natural characters of g, where ġ is the image of g in D_Q:
- det g = the character with kernel D_Q^+;
- sg g = χ_C(ġ), with kernel V_S;
- det g · sg g = χ_D(ġ), with kernel V_A.
It also announces a lattice diagram of subgroups, (28) on the next page, and sets Z = Cent(Gl_Λ(M)) = Cent(Sl_Λ(M)) as (27).

Purpose: a complete, canonical description of the finite group GL_2(Z/4) and its normal subgroups. These control level-4 structures on elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, i.e. the covering X(4) → X(2) → X(1) and its intermediate quotients.
errors: No mathematical errors detected. The checks hold: |Gl| = 96, |Sl| = 48, Sl_ab ≅ Z/4, [Sl, Sl] = A_4 of order 12, Gl_ab ≅ (Z/2)^2, and Cent(GL_2(Z/4)) = Cent(SL_2(Z/4)) = {±1}.
Notational slip: 'Gl(M) → D_Q' in Corollary 2 omits the subscript Λ.
Unlabeled step: the arrow Z → z_Q being an isomorphism (the image of −id is the central element e_Q of D_Q) is used without comment. It holds because −id ∉ A_4 = kernel.

ideas.what: Exact-sequence 'star' for SL_2(Z/4): extensions by A_4, by the centre ±1, and by A_4 × ±1, with quotients S_4, Z/4 and ±1
ideas.modern_name: Structure of SL_2(Z/4Z); SL_2(Z/4)/A_4 ≅ Z/4 abelianization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical finite group theory / modular curves literature (e.g. the abelianization of SL_2(Z) being Z/12)

ideas.what: GL_2(Z/4)/A_4 ≅ dihedral group D_4 of order 8, defined canonically via a quadratic form Q; hence GL_2(Z/4)_ab ≅ D_4 mod centre ≅ F_2 × F_2 canonically
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; well known in the study of X(4) and 2-adic Galois images of elliptic curves (e.g. Rouse–Zureick-Brown)

ideas.what: Identification of the three index-2 characters of GL_2(Z/4) (det, sign of the S_4-image, and their product) with the three characters of D_Q

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, coordinate-free bookkeeping of the subgroup structure of GL_2(Z/4)/SL_2(Z/4), all classical facts. The only distinctive feature is the canonical, choice-free framing through the affine plane I and the quadratic form Q. That fits Grothendieck's style but is not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The central group in diagram (25) is 𝔖l_Λ(M) = Sl_Λ(M), not Gl_Λ(M).
The top object is 𝔖_I^+ × {1, −id_M}; the transcription has 𝔖_I^*.
'{F_2^? Q} ≃ F_2' should read '{1, e_Q} ≃ F_2', the centre z_Q of D_Q (cf. next page: z_Q = {1, e_ω}).
The vertical arrow from Sl_Λ(M) to {±1} is labelled 'cont' (or similar); it is not det. The left arrows are Sl → 𝔖_I →sg {±1}, and the right arrows are Sl → D_Q^+ → {±1}.
In the NB, the first line is det g = χ_?(ġ), with a crossed-out symbol, for the character whose kernel is D_Q^+. The phrase 'pour g ∈ Gl(M)' is accompanied by 'ġ im. can. ∈ D_Q'.
The marginal note under (D_Q)_ab reads 'vectoriel de rang 2 sur F_2 et même can. isom. : F_2 × F_2'.
